subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.com>, Jesse Lee <jesse.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Key pain points we heard
- Latency spikes on your customer-facing chat that cause a poor UX for short interactions (~200–400ms target).
- High per-token costs on peak hours due to repeated prompt patterns and long context windows.
- Need for structured outputs for downstream order-processing system (JSON payloads with strict schema).

Goals you confirmed
- Sub-250ms 95th percentile for simple 1–3 turn chat flows.
- Reduce per-conversation token cost by ~30% through caching/batching and quantized model variants.
- Deliver a structured response (order_confirmation JSON) and an embeddings-based reranking step for knowledge retrieval.

Integration & product fit notes
- SDK: You prefer the hosted SDK (Node + Python) with a lightweight client on the browser for streaming. We discussed a small client-side change to switch to Redwood's streaming tokenizer to reduce perceived latency.
- Function calling: We recommended using Redwood's structured function-calling API for the order_confirmation payload so your app can reliably parse and validate outputs.
- Streaming: We'll enable server-side streaming + client incremental render to hit your UX targets.
- Structured outputs: Suggest pinning a response schema and using Redwood's schema validation hook to detect regressions during rollouts.
- Embeddings / reranking: We suggested an embeddings + reranker flow: dense embeddings for candidate retrieval, then a lightweight reranker model (quantized variant) served on Dedicated pool for cheap rerank latency.

Proposed next steps (timeline)
1) Redwood to send a 2-week MVP integration plan and SDK change log — ACTION: Marissa (today EOD).
2) Acme to share a small sample of chat prompts + one canonical order schema — ACTION: Sam (by Fri, Jul 2).
3) Schedule a 60-min PoC kickoff with Neha (solutions) and Lukas (security) — ACTION: Jesse to propose slots (next week).
4) Kick off a 2-week PoC: focus on streaming integration + structured outputs + a basic reranker evaluation.

Attachments referenced
- Redwood_MVP_integration_plan.pdf (high-level tasks, milestones, owners)
- redwood-sdk-change-log.txt (high-level SDK diff we discussed)

If I missed anything or mis-stated priorities, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll circulate the MVP plan and proposed PoC dates later today.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jesse Lee <jesse.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks, Marissa — solid summary. A few clarifications/questions: 

1) Latency targets: The 250ms target is for the simplest confirmation flows (single-turn). For the 1–3 turn flows we care most about 95th < 400ms. Can you call out which of Redwood's deployment modes you expect to hit those numbers on (hosted vs dedicated)?

2) Reranking: For cost reasons we'd like the reranker to run after a small candidate set (<= 25). Will the default embedding + ANN index work with that constraint?

3) Security/compliance: We need to confirm what audit logs and retention options are available in the PoC; Lukas (security) will need to review.

We can share the prompt samples and the canonical order schema by Friday. For the PoC kickoff, Jesse will send a few times — aiming for Jul 6 or Jul 7.

Two small asks: 
- Please include an estimate of incremental cost for a dedicated reranker node (per-hour) in the MVP plan.
- Can you mark which SDK changes are breaking vs additive in the change log?

Appreciate it — looking forward to the PoC.

—Sam
Sam Taylor
Product Lead, Conversational Commerce
Acme Corp
sam.taylor@acme.com | (650) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.com>, Jesse Lee <jesse.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Sam. Quick answers inline and updated next steps: 

1) Latency by deployment mode:
- Hosted (Redwood API): for small single-turn responses we commonly hit ~150–220ms p50 and ~300–450ms p95 depending on model/region. Good candidate for initial PoC to validate streaming UX.
- Dedicated: predictable sub-400ms p95 for 1–3 turn flows once provisioned and tuned; recommended if you need SLA guarantees and predictable unit economics.

I’ll call out both numbers and recommended option for your scale in the MVP plan.

2) Reranking after candidate set <=25: yes — that matches our suggested flow. Our embeddings + ANN retrieval (Faiss/HNSW) works well for small candidate sets; reranker costs remain low because it's only scoring the 25 items per request. I’ll include cost per 1k requests and an example compute estimate for a Dedicated small GPU node in the plan.

3) Security/compliance: Lukas — looping you in here. For the PoC we can enable audit logging, limited retention, and encrypted keys (KMS). Neha will coordinate a short security checklist for the kickoff.

Updated timeline / immediate next steps
- Today EOD: I’ll post the MVP integration plan + SDK change log to the Drive link and HubSpot (see links below).
- Fri Jul 2: Acme shares prompt samples and canonical order schema (Sam).
- Jul 6–7: PoC kickoff (Jesse to confirm times).
- Jul 8–22: 2-week PoC: streaming + structured outputs + reranker evaluation.

Attachments + links

Thanks — talk soon.
